dedupe_keys.name: debris impact resistance of building assemblies ttu florida a m fsu and uf test compilation for nist 2006

description: A summary report, submitted to the National Institute of Standards and Technology in August 2006, that compiles laboratory tests of how well wall and roof assemblies resist windborne debris. The tests were done by the Wind Science and Engineering Research Center at Texas Tech University, and by Florida A&M University, Florida State University and the University of Florida for the Florida Division of Emergency Management, under the NIST and Texas Tech cooperative Windstorm Mitigation Initiative. Missile types, weights and speeds were set for each storm type and classification, for example the Texas Tech large missile test that fires a 15 lb 2 by 4 in. board at 100 mph to represent tornado winds up to 250 mph, and the hurricane missile test used in building codes. The report lists assemblies built from commonly available materials that resisted debris for a given storm and speed, and its appendix holds the test results. Coverage: the United States. Format and access: a free PDF of 62 pages on the Texas Tech site. Licence: none stated. Caveats: results are pass or fail by assembly and missile class, an old snapshot that has not been updated, and the Clemson University data are excluded because of different criteria. It gives fragility evidence for vulnerability curves and safe room and code studies of tornado and hurricane damage; related records are not yet linked.
